slots.title: References Connecting Blast Loading to Saturated-Tailings Response
slots.instruction: Identify peer-reviewed papers, technical manuals, or authoritative tailings/dam references that connect blast-induced vibration or short-duration transient dynamic loading to excess pore-pressure generation, cyclic mobility, or liquefaction in saturated sands, silts, mine tailings, or fine tailings. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Model Families and Equations
slots.instruction: Describe the model families or equations used to relate cyclic stress or cyclic strain demand, number of equivalent cycles, drainage conditions, and material state to excess pore-pressure ratio or liquefaction triggering. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Frequency, Duration, and Short High-Frequency Pulses
slots.instruction: Explain how the cited methods treat loading frequency, duration, and short high-frequency pulses, including the limits stated when earthquake-derived cyclic-liquefaction concepts are applied to blast-like loading. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Material Parameters and Motion-Record Limits
slots.instruction: Identify the material parameters required to evaluate pore-pressure generation or cyclic resistance in saturated tailings, and distinguish which of those parameters cannot be inferred from acceleration or velocity records alone. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Conservative Report Wording
slots.instruction: Provide conservative wording for a report that evaluates blast-record scenarios as dynamic demand indicators rather than as a calibrated pore-pressure or liquefaction prediction model. Write in flowing paragraphs.

constraints: Prepare the response for an English technical report.
